## Changes

- Polished the interface while retaining Azuria’s layout, pink-and-blue theme and right-hand Discover filters.
- Standardised Library sorting and grouping with themed, keyboard-accessible dropdowns.
- Improved supporting-text readability, control sizing and card consistency, with calmer hover effects and notification shadows.
- Replaced promotional wording with clearer descriptions and simplified the empty-library screen.
- Added a keyboard Skip to content link and clearer account progress and update errors.
- Made settings actions wrap when space is limited. Success notices now clear after five seconds or navigation; errors remain visible until dismissed.

## Update information

Install through Settings → Update & restart.

This update does not change saved instances, accounts or the database schema. Discover remains a fictional catalogue preview with installation disabled. Microsoft/Minecraft application-access review remains pending; game installation and launching remain in development.

## Changes

- Moved Discover filters into a separate right-hand sidebar, with catalogue results on the left.
- Added a pink accent, clearer filter grouping and independently scrollable controls while preserving Azuria’s blue selection states.
- Adjusted the layout for dark and light themes and the minimum desktop window size.
- Preserved local search, filters, sorting and pagination across all four content categories.

## Update information

Install through Settings → Update & restart, then open Discover from the sidebar.

The catalogue still uses clearly labelled fictional example projects, creators and statistics. Live provider searches, downloads and installation are not connected; Install buttons remain disabled.

This update does not change saved instances or accounts. Microsoft/Minecraft application-access review remains pending; game installation and launching remain in development.

## Changes

- Added a Discover catalogue preview for modpacks, mods, datapacks and resource packs.
- Added working local search, source/category/loader/version filters, sorting, result limits and pagination.
- Added compact project rows, original gradient icons and themed dropdowns using Azuria’s pink-and-blue styling.
- Supported dark and light themes, including the minimum desktop window size.
- Kept the development roadmap available through the help button.

## Update information

Install through Settings → Update & restart, then open Discover from the sidebar.

The catalogue currently contains clearly labelled fictional example projects, creators and statistics. Live provider searches, downloads and installation are not connected; Install buttons are disabled.

This update does not change the instance database or saved accounts. Microsoft/Minecraft application-access review remains pending; game installation and launching remain in development.

## Changes

- Fixed Sign in with Microsoft opening Documents or File Explorer instead of the default browser on Windows.
- Opened the complete Microsoft authorization URL through Windows’ registered browser handler, preserving its PKCE and callback parameters.
- Added browser-opening error checks so failed launches show a retryable error in Azuria.

## Update information

Install through Settings → Update & restart, then retry Settings → Minecraft account → Sign in with Microsoft. Cancel any previous pending sign-in first.

This update does not change saved instances, the database schema or stored account credentials. Your default browser should open the Microsoft sign-in page.

This is a development release. Live Microsoft/Xbox/Minecraft sign-in still requires verification with Azuria’s Entra registration. Game installation and Minecraft launching remain in development.

## Changes

- Added Microsoft sign-in through your default browser with secure PKCE authentication.
- Added Minecraft account controls in Settings: sign in, reconnect, switch account, cancel and sign out.
- Added Xbox authentication, Java Edition entitlement checks and Minecraft profile verification.
- Saved refresh credentials securely in Windows Credential Manager, with automatic reconnection at startup.
- Added clear progress and errors for expired sessions, account restrictions, connection failures and Minecraft Services access issues.
- Preserved the previous account when switching fails or is cancelled, and retained rotated refresh credentials when later verification fails.
- Linked the sidebar and library account controls to account settings while preserving Azuria’s existing theme.

## Update information

Install through Settings → Update & restart, then open Settings → Minecraft account to sign in. This update does not change the instance database schema.

Sign-in requires the Windows desktop app and a personal Microsoft account with Minecraft Java Edition access. Signing out removes Azuria’s saved account; your browser may remain signed in to Microsoft.

This is a development release. Live Minecraft Services access for Azuria’s client ID still requires verification. The Entra registration must support personal Microsoft accounts and a desktop http://localhost redirect. Game installation and Minecraft launching remain in development.

## Changes

- Updated the Windows application icon with the supplied pink Azuria artwork.
- Updated the launcher header mark and browser-preview favicon to match.
- Preserved the artwork’s transparency and proportions across the generated icon sizes.

## Update information

Install through Settings → Update & restart. Windows may briefly retain the previous icon in its shortcut or taskbar cache; reopening the launcher or recreating a pinned shortcut can refresh it.

This is a development release. Microsoft sign-in, game installation and Minecraft launching are not implemented yet.
